Oriel had never trusted the river, not since the summer it claimed her brother's boat. Now she stood on the jetty with a lantern, watching the mist roll in from the far bank. Behind her, the village slumbered; only the baker's chimney exhaled a thin grey line into the night. She thought of Teodor and the promise she had made him, and of the map folded in her pocket. When the bell at the chapel tolled three, she untied the skiff and pushed off into the current.
